parakeet: The Gospels present radical personal moral demands, nonviolence, total generosity, limitless forgiveness without any corresponding political, economic, or institutional framework to make those demands just, reciprocal, or sustainable. Ethics are intensified, but structures are left untouched. Jesus demands moral extremes from individuals, not systems. We can start with non-resistance to harm. We've all heard the scripture turn the other cheek, but let's actually read it in context. Matthew chapter five, verse thirty-nine is do not resist an evil person. If anyone slaps you on the right cheek, turn to them the other cheek also. Do not resist an evil person. Do not resist, turn the other cheek. There's no discussion of power imbalance, repeat abuse, collective defense, or justice for victims. The burden is entirely on the harmed person. But Jesus also advocates for total economic surrender. In the Gospel of Luke, chapter 12, verse 33, he's heard telling people to sell your possessions and give to the poor. In chapter 14 of the same book, he says, Those of you who do not give up everything you have cannot be my disciples. There is no accompanying system for resource redistribution, protection from exploitation, economic reciprocity, or safeguards against poverty. Generosity then is moralized while poverty is privatized.
